paragraphs.source_en: Einstein came to this realization between 1916 and 1918, when he used the newly fashioned equations of general relativity to show that- much as electric charges racing up and down a broadcast antenna produce electromagnetic waves (this is how radio and television waves are produced) -matter racing this way and that (as in a supernova explosion) produces gravitational waves. And since gravity is curvature, a gravitational wave is a wave of curvature. paragraphs.source_en: versy, at least in part because of overadherence to Machian philosophy. If general relativity fully incorporated Mach's ideas, then the "geometry of space" would merely be a convenient language for expressing the location and motion of one massive object with respect to another. Empty space, in this way of thinking, would be an empty concept, so how could it be sensible to speak of empty space wiggling? Many physicists tried to prove that the supposed waves in space amounted to a misinterpretation of the mathematics of general relativity. But in due course, the theoretical analyses converged on the correct conclusion: gravitational waves are real, and space can ripple.
